rationale: Both have the same mutex-protected design with the counters embedded in a combined readWriteCounter. B has more descriptive field names and uses defer in the getters, which is slightly more idiomatic. However, B counts an operation only when n > 0. A Read or Write call that returns zero bytes, for example with an error or at EOF, is still an IO operation, so B silently undercounts operations, which matters for the billing use case. A counts every call, which matches the requirement to report the total number of read/write operations. A's terse field names (n, nop) and its type assertions when reusing the constructors in NewReadWriteCounter are minor style weaknesses. Correct semantics outweighs them, so A is the better solution.
